prompt: Write the ORM-style mapper that turns raw database rows of Objects into Customer records, defaulting every missing or blank column. Complete toCustomer and toCustomers.
explanation: A JDBC row hands you Objects that may be null for any column, so a mapper is mostly null-handling plus a cast to the type the column really holds. Doing that work in one place means the rest of the program deals with a proper Customer record and never has to think about nulls or casts again -- this is the core job of every object-relational mapper. Note that unboxing a null Integer throws a NullPointerException, which is exactly why the null test has to come before the cast.
hints: Read each column into an Object variable first, test it for null, and only then cast it -- (Integer) rawId on a null would be fine, but unboxing it to int would throw.
For the name, trim first and then test isEmpty(); that way a value of "   " is treated as blank just like a missing column.
toCustomers is a plain loop that calls toCustomer for each row, with an early return of the empty list when rows is null.
